samples.question: The picture contains exactly two dark cords in two far-apart parts of the image, and the two cords never touch each other. Each cord is a single unbranched stroke of constant thickness with two free ends. On each cord one end is covered by a black square, which marks that cord's start; the other end is bare. Each cord carries exactly three disks sitting on it, one red, one green and one blue, so every colour appears once on each cord. On a given cord, walk along the stroke from that cord's black start square towards its bare end and number the disks 1, 2 and 3 in the order you meet them; that number is the disk's position on that cord. The two cords may have very different total lengths and different disk spacings, and only the order of meeting counts, not any distance. Exactly one colour has the same position number on both cords, and the other two colours have their two position numbers exchanged. Which colour has the same position number on both cords? Answer red, green, or blue.
